newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela PdVSA chief defends out-sourcing.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela PdVSA chief defends out-sourcing.

text.p: Venezuelan state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela's (PdVSA) policy of out-sourcing non-essential operations did not imperil workers' conditions, PdVSA President Luis Giusti said Tuesday.

"Out-sourcing is always done with full respect of collective worker's contracts and only after careful study that it does not hurt human resource policies," he told Reuters after a meeting in Congress.

Venezuela's leading oil workers' union Fedepetrol threatened Thursday to strike over PdVSA's policy of out-sourcing some health, computing, electrical and transport operations to private companies as part of its oil opening strategy.
Fedepetrol says the policy will lead to a "de-nationalisation of the oil industry" as well as worsening working conditions.
"I have to ask myself what is denationalisation," said Giusti. "We have to rid ourselves of this kind of dogmatism. Here people talk about sovereignty but all that happens is people get poorer."

Venezuela's oil unions are due to meet Thursday to firm a common position they will then present to PdVSA next Tuesday. Fedepetrol secretary general Carlos Ortega has said oil workers may strike if PdVSA fails to provide satisfactory answers to a long list of complaints.
"Third parties can carry out these activities which, by opening up possibilities for private capital, also expands the base of Venezuelan business," Giusti added.
